title: Maintaining Proper Pipe Slope for Waste Flow
description: Correct pipe slope is critical for long-term drainage health and system reliability. Horizontal drainage piping relies on gravity to transport both liquids and solid materials efficiently. If the pitch is too flat, water velocity drops, allowing heavy organic solids and grease to settle on the pipe invert and form persistent blockages. Conversely, excessive pitch can cause liquids to rush ahead, leaving solids behind. Regular maintenance inspections using a precision torpedo level ensure horizontal runs maintain consistent slope without sagging sections or water bellies that collect debris over time.

Maintaining Proper Pipe Slope for Waste Flow

Correct pipe slope is critical for long-term drainage health and system reliability. Horizontal drainage piping relies on gravity to transport both liquids and solid materials efficiently. If the pitch is too flat, water velocity drops, allowing heavy organic solids and grease to settle on the pipe invert and form persistent blockages. Conversely, excessive pitch can cause liquids to rush ahead, leaving solids behind. Regular maintenance inspections using a precision torpedo level ensure horizontal runs maintain consistent slope without sagging sections or water bellies that collect debris over time.
